#### Goal

The goal of the pilot study assignment is to develop a preliminary research question and to collect some initial data, both in preparation for your Island project.

#### To Turn In

In your RStudio Project folder, in `islands-paper.qmd`:

- Introduction: 1-2 paragraphs of background, ending with your research question (1–2 sentences) and hypothesis
- Methods: study design, participants and sampling, and variables

In [Canvas](https://cofi.instructure.com/courses/18743/assignments/244939):

- Upload both your `islands-paper.qmd` file and the rendered PDF (`islands-paper.pdf`). You must upload both files at every checkpoint.
- Link to Google Sheet with data  
- If you are working in a group, who is in it (one submission per group)  
:::

## Preliminaries

- Review [the Islands tips](project-islands-tips.qmd) document.
- Work through **your own login** to the Islands (in a group, each member can use their own login and combine data, or you can share one, but the group must agree on one study).  
- Use **your own (or your group's) Google Sheet** for data (tidy format: one row per person, one column per variable).  
- Use one **RStudio Project folder** for writing (your own, or one shared by your group).

## Research Question

-   Develop a question that is **interesting** and **feasible**.  
-   You may use the **PICO** structure (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome).
    -   [Description](https://guides.mclibrary.duke.edu/ebm/pico)
    -   [Sample PICO questions](https://libraryguides.nau.edu/c.php?g=665927&p=4682772)
-   Questions can be **experimental** or **observational**.

**Final form:** 1–2 sentences describing the population, treatment/exposure, comparison, and outcome.

## Design a Study

- Read [this guide to study design](https://www.cebm.ox.ac.uk/files/testing/cebm-study-design-april-20131.pdf) from the Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (University of Oxford).
- Design a study to answer your research question.
    - Describe how subjects will be selected.  
    - Random sampling is not required, but if you do not use it you must justify representativeness.  
    - Response variable must be **quantitative**.  
    - Primary explanatory variable may be either **quantitative** or **categorical**
    - Collect at least **four** additional **demographic variables** that you think may confound your results (at least two must be numeric).  


### Preliminary Data Collection

Using your study design, measure **at least 20 islanders** for a pilot study storing your results in a google sheet.


## Introduction

Write 1-2 paragraphs that move from general to specific:

- Find at least two research papers related to your research question.
- Why does this topic matter? What is plausible or already known (you can draw on what you learn on the Islands)?
- What is your research question, and what do you hypothesize?
- Make sure you reference and cite these papers in your Introduction.

End with your research question from above.

## Methods Section

In the Methods section of your paper, clearly describe the following in your methods section:

- Study design (e.g., experimental, case-control, cohort)  
- Target population  
- Inclusion/exclusion criteria 
- Sampling methods  
- Explanatory variable
- Outcome (numeric response variable)  
- Demographic variables (≥4 total, ≥2 numeric)  
- Randomization and blinding methods (if applicable)  

You will add your sample size justification and statistical analysis plan to Methods in later checkpoints.

Write clearly and concisely without repetition.


## Grading Rubric

This checkpoint is worth **15 points**, which is 1.875% of your course grade (the four interim checkpoints together make up 30% of the project, and the project is 25% of the course). Pilot checkpoints are graded mainly on completeness and on how well the work sets up the rest of your paper, and you will get written feedback to use in later checkpoints. The criteria mirror the Introduction and Methods criteria in the [final project rubric](project-rubric.qmd).

| Criteria | Full credit | Points |
|:---|:---|:---:|
| **Research question and hypothesis** | The question is 1-2 sentences, names the population, exposure or treatment, comparison, and outcome, and is both interesting and feasible on the Islands. A hypothesis is stated and matches the question. | 0-3 |
| **Introduction** | 1-2 paragraphs that move from general to specific and explain why the topic matters. Draws on at least two research papers, both cited in the text with a reference list. Ends with the research question. | 0-3 |
| **Methods: design and sampling** | Study design (experimental or observational), target population, inclusion/exclusion criteria, sampling method (with a justification of representativeness if not random), and randomization and blinding (if applicable) are described with enough detail that someone else could replicate the study. | 0-4 |
| **Methods: variables** | The numeric response, the primary explanatory variable, and at least four demographic variables (at least two numeric) are each defined, with units or levels. Demographic variables are plausibly related to confounding. | 0-2 |
| **Pilot data** | The linked Google Sheet is viewable by the instructor, includes at least 20 islanders, and is tidy (one row per person, one column per variable) with clear column names matching the Methods. | 0-2 |
| **Submission and writing** | Both `islands-paper.qmd` and the rendered `islands-paper.pdf` are uploaded, group members are listed (if applicable), and the writing is clear, concise, and free of repetition and major typos. | 0-1 |
| **Total** | | **15** |

### What the point levels look like

- **Full credit:** meets every element in the "Full credit" column.
- **Partial credit:** an element is present but vague, incomplete, or inconsistent with the rest of the paper (for example, a research question with no clear comparison, or a variable listed in Methods that is missing from the data).
- **No credit:** the element is missing.

If a requirement is not met (for example, fewer than 20 islanders, or a categorical response variable), you will be asked to fix it before the Power checkpoint, since the later checkpoints build directly on this data.
